blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C1):** eu consigo escrever um e-mail formal de reclamação com objetivo claro, detalhes e pedido de ação, a partir de uma notícia.

body: Esta aula treina **responder em frases completas (IELTS Speaking, TOEFL Speaking)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.headline: Report: Residents’ Emails Persuade Council to Fix Street Lights
paras: After more than 300 formal emails from residents of Marsh Lane, the city council has agreed to **replace** broken street lights by June. “Each message **stated its purpose** clearly, **elaborated** on the danger and **requested** a date,” said councillor Ines Prado. “**Having been given** such precise information, we could act.”
Residents had been complaining for two years. One email, quoted at the meeting, began: “**I am writing to** draw your attention to…” and ended: “I would be grateful for a written reply by 15 May.”

items.q: Residents sent more than 300 formal emails.
The council refuses to replace the lights.

blocks.body: Reclamação formal: **fatos + impacto + pedido concreto com prazo**, em tom firme, mas educado. Sem acusações pessoais.
Evite *You never do anything!*; prefira *I would be grateful if…*

items.s: I am ___ to draw your attention to a problem. (write)
Three lights have not ___ since March. (work)
I would be ___ for a written reply. (grateful)
We close with “Yours ___” when we do not know the name. (faithfully)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

body: **I am writing to draw your attention to…** — Escrevo para chamar sua atenção para…
**I wish to lodge a complaint.** — Desejo registrar uma reclamação.
**I would be grateful for a written reply.** — Agradeceria uma resposta por escrito.
**Failing that,…** — Caso contrário,…
**This is not acceptable.** — Isto não é aceitável.
**I look forward to your swift response.** — Aguardo sua rápida resposta.
**Yours faithfully,** — Atenciosamente (sem nome),
**At the earliest opportunity** — Na primeira oportunidade
**Shall we send one email or many?** — Mandamos um e-mail ou vários?
**Should we be angry?** — Devemos ser raivosos?
**No. Firm, but courteous.** — Não. Firmes, mas corteses.

blocks.title: Residents’ meeting
lines: Shall we send one email or many?
Many. Each should state its purpose and request a date.
Vários. Cada um deve declarar seu objetivo e pedir uma data.

items.label: Expressividade
items.note: Expressividade: varie altura, volume e velocidade para mostrar atitude; uma voz monótona soa desinteressada, mesmo com boas palavras.
words: That is NOT what I meant.

prompts.q: State the purpose of a complaint.
prompts.model: I am writing to draw your attention to broken street lights.
I would be grateful if you could replace them by 15 May.
This has made the street unsafe at night.

blocks.task: Write a complete formal complaint email (8–10 sentences) about a real or imaginary local problem.
blocks.model: Subject: Broken lights on Marsh Lane. Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing to draw your attention to three broken street lights on Marsh Lane. Since March they have not worked. This has made the street unsafe at night, especially for older residents. Having reported the problem twice, I have received no reply. I would be grateful if you could repair the lights by 15 May. Could you also confirm the date in writing? Please find attached photographs. Thank you for your consideration. Yours faithfully, Marina Costa

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
